story.vex: A target on paper means nothing until reality tests it. Let's test it. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED before it started: every recovery event is checked honestly against the plan's own targets. Astro: "The plan is only as good as what it actually does under pressure."

files./home/cadet/citadel/README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Read dr-plan.txt for the targets, then recovery-log.txt for three real events. Classify each event as within-target or exceeded-target.

1. cat dr-plan.txt
2. cat recovery-log.txt
3. echo <event> <answer> >> findings.txt   (answer: within-target | exceeded-target)
files./home/cadet/citadel/dr-plan.txt:
DISASTER RECOVERY PLAN — Targets
------------------------------------
RTO (recovery time objective): 4 hours
RPO (recovery point objective): 1 hour
files./home/cadet/citadel/recovery-log.txt:
RECOVERY LOG
--------------
event-relay-drill      down 3 hours, backup was 30 minutes old at time of failure
event-shield-outage    down 6 hours, backup was 20 minutes old at time of failure
event-storage-failure  down 2 hours, backup was 90 minutes old at time of failure

steps.title: Read the plan and the log
steps.body: Astro: "Know the targets before you judge the events." `cat dr-plan.txt`, then `cat recovery-log.txt`.

steps.title: Check each event against the targets
steps.body: Astro: "Downtime under 4 hours and data loss under 1 hour both meet target. Either one exceeded is a miss." Classify all three events. Write each answer as one line in findings.txt: `echo <item> <answer> >> findings.txt`.
